questions.title: Does a €300 service-desk voucher 'in lieu of compensation' offset 14C's €600?
questions.found: On 24 Jan the T2 service desk issued passenger 14C (NS31) a €300 voucher 'in lieu of compensation'. CRM records it as accepted; her claim says she never agreed. There is no signed acceptance on file.
questions.why_flagged: Sources disagree (CRM vs. the passenger's claim), and Art. 7(3) needs signed acceptance for an offset. No precedent for unsigned in-lieu vouchers.
questions.recommends: No signed acceptance, no offset: pay €600 cash; the voucher stays as goodwill.
questions.recommended_option: Pay €600 cash; the voucher stays as goodwill
options: Pay €600 cash; the voucher stays as goodwill
Ask 14C to sign the acceptance first

evidence.quote: I never agreed to take a voucher instead of my compensation and I did not sign anything

questions.title: Is the return sector of a storm-cancelled rotation extraordinary when both ends were calm?
questions.found: NS113 (LIS–DUB), NS115 (FCO–DUB) and NS117 (MUC–DUB) were cancelled because their outbound legs NS112, NS114 and NS116 never left Dublin. Each return was calm at both ends: e.g. NS117, Munich calm at STD 14:05Z and Dublin 11 kt at STA 16:20Z, after the 02:30–15:00Z window.
questions.why_flagged: No precedent. C-74/19 (previous rotation) needs a direct causal link and reasonable measures. No spare tail within 3 h: NS117's earliest ferry ex-DUB 15:30Z → MUC dep 18:25Z = STD+4h20. Passengers were offered the earliest reroute (LH via FRA).
questions.recommends: Extraordinary only if no aircraft and crew could operate the return within 3 h of STD and passengers were offered the earliest reroute on any carrier (C-74/19).
questions.recommended_option: Extraordinary if no aircraft within 3 h of STD and the earliest reroute was offered
options: Extraordinary if no aircraft within 3 h of STD and the earliest reroute was offered
Not extraordinary: compensation owed on all three
